description: Only lab records with total cholesterol strictly above 180 pass the filter; records with exactly 180 are excluded.

a.request: For lab records that match a patient by ID (unmatched records dropped) and have total cholesterol (`T-CHO`) strictly greater than 180, break them down by patient sex (`SEX`), keeping each recorded value, including a blank one, as its own group. For each group, show the sex, the average anti-DNA level (`Laboratory.DNA`), and the average of albumin minus total protein (`ALB` − `TP`), ignoring missing values and leaving the average empty if there are none, unrounded.
a.sql: SELECT P.SEX, AVG(L.DNA) AS avg_dna, AVG(L.ALB - L.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory L INNER JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID WHERE L.`T-CHO` > 180 GROUP BY P.SEX

b.request: Lab records joined to patients by ID (inner join, so unmatched records are dropped) are kept only if total cholesterol `T-CHO` is strictly greater than 180, so records with exactly 180 are excluded. They are grouped by patient `SEX`, with each value including blank as its own group, and each group shows the sex, the unrounded average of `Laboratory.DNA`, and the unrounded average of (`ALB` − `TP`), ignoring missing values and returning NULL if there are none.
b.sql: SELECT P.SEX, AVG(L.DNA) AS avg_dna, AVG(L.ALB - L.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory AS L INNER JOIN Patient AS P ON L.ID = P.ID WHERE L.`T-CHO` > 180 GROUP BY P.SEX
b.raw: Lab records joined to patients by ID (inner join, so unmatched records are dropped) are kept only if total cholesterol `T-CHO` is strictly greater than 180, so records with exactly 180 are excluded. d.request: Inner-join Laboratory records to Patient on ID (dropping unmatched records), keep only records with `T-CHO` strictly greater than 180 (exactly 180 excluded), group by `Patient.SEX` with each distinct value including blank/empty as its own group, and for each group return `SEX`, the unrounded average of `Laboratory.DNA`, and the unrounded average of (`ALB` − `TP`), ignoring missing values and returning NULL if none exist.
d.sql: SELECT P.SEX AS SEX, AVG(L.DNA) AS avg_DNA, AVG(L.ALB - L.TP) AS avg_ALB_minus_TP FROM Laboratory AS L INNER JOIN Patient AS P ON L.ID = P.ID WHERE L.`T-CHO` > 180 GROUP BY P.SEX

c.request: For lab records that match a patient by ID (unmatched records dropped), screened with 180 as the total cholesterol (`T-CHO`) cutoff, break them down by patient sex (`SEX`), keeping each recorded value, including a blank one, as its own group. For each group, show the sex, the average anti-DNA level (`Laboratory.DNA`), and the average of albumin minus total protein (`ALB` − `TP`), ignoring missing values and leaving the average empty if there are none, unrounded. Only lab records with total cholesterol strictly above 180 pass the filter; records with exactly 180 are excluded.
c.sql: SELECT p.SEX, AVG(l.DNA) AS avg_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` > 180 GROUP BY p.SEX
